request.system:
You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

<<<

ASX ANNOUNCEMENT
Tuesday, 20 October 2026
NAB simplifying operating model and improving alignment
to customer priorities
National Australia Bank today announced actions to simplify its operating model and better align its
workforce to prioritise growth and technology initiatives for customers.
NAB is implementing these changes as part of a broader review to identify the nature of the workforce
required to support NAB’s strategic ambition in an evolving operating environment.
These actions will help to make NAB a stronger bank, better placed to navigate risks and
opportunities arising from more challenging economic conditions, increasing customer expectations,
competitive intensity and rapid technological change.
They create capacity for ongoing investment in NAB’s strategic ambition for customers and support
priorities to grow business banking, drive deposit growth and strengthen proprietary home lending.
As part of these actions, NAB expects to reduce its internal workforce by up to 2,500 roles or ~6%
in FY27. This will include up to 1,500 roles before the end of 2026. NAB will also materially reduce
its use of consultants and external contractors.
NAB Group CEO, Andrew Irvine said: “Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will
improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank.
“These changes are expected to improve outcomes for customers by reducing duplication and
speeding up decision making.
“We are particularly focused on reducing the size of corporate functions. There will be no material
impact to customer-facing banking roles.
“We have also deliberately made deeper changes to senior management positions which will
broaden leadership responsibilities across the bank.
“This will simplify work between teams and improve cross-functional processes with clearer roles,
priorities and accountabilities for our colleagues.
“We know this will be a difficult period for our colleagues impacted by these changes as well as the
people around them. We will treat every person with dignity and respect.”

Colleague support
NAB will commence consultation with colleagues and the Finance Sector Union. Consistent with
established organisational change processes, NAB will support departing colleagues with:
• Consultation and engagement opportunities.
• Redeployment and reskilling opportunities.
• Career transition support.
• Redundancy entitlements in accordance with applicable industrial instruments and
employment obligations.
Restructuring charge
NAB expects to recognise a restructuring charge of approximately $300m pre-tax in FY27. The
charge relates to redundancy, redeployment and organisational redesign costs. This compares with
a charge of approximately $80m pre-tax which has been incurred in each of FY25 and FY26.
Further details on the cost outlook for FY27 will be provided with the release of FY26 results on 5
November 2026.
